rows: The strong thunderstorm winds knocked down a large tree limb.
Fourteen telephone poles were blown down. Several trees were also knocked down due to the severe thunderstorm wind gust.
A tornado was reported near the McCulloch County line. The twister remained over open fields. This tornado crossed into McCulloch County.
This large hail broke the windows of a house.
Power lines were knocked down and garbage dumpsters were turned over.
Many tree limbs were blown down.
Strong winds damaged a the roof of a barn with the wind speed estimated at 60 mph or more. Dime to nickel size hail was also reported.
Quarter size hail was reported 8 miles north of Menard.
Quarter size hail was reported along U.S. 190 about 8 miles west of Menard.
Dime to quarter size hail was reported in Menard.
The golf ball size hail lasted for 30 minutes.
The public reported golf ball size hail in Erna.
Law enforcement offiicials reported numerous cars damaged along U.S. Highway 83 about 5 miles north of Menard.
The Menard Fire Chief reported baseball size hail on Ranch Road 2092.
A trained spotter reported golf ball to tennis size hail which lasted approximately 5 minutes.
A rainfall network observer reported hen size hail and a car windshield destroyed about 11 miles south southwest of Hext.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported at Fort McKavett State Park.
A National Weather Service Cooperative Observer reported numerous large tree limbs of 40 feet in length were downed by the damaging winds. The strong winds also ripped up some metal from a building.
A few mesquite tree limbs were broken by the damaging winds about 1 mile west of London near FM 370.
The public reported golf ball size hail at the intersection of Saline Road and 1 mile north of U.S. Highway 377.
Strong thunderstorm winds lifted a hunting stand and uprooted a large live oak tree. The oak tree also blocked the roadway.
This large hail broke out a bedroom window. The hail was just under tennis ball size hail but larger than an egg.

Texas Tech West Texas Mesonet Station located 2 miles northwest of Menard measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 64 mph.

A mesonet observation station measured a 60 mph wind gust.
A CoCoRaHS observer reported quarter size hail from occasionally 715 PM to until 830 PM.

Delayed Report: The NWS conducted a storm survey. There was damage to 8 power poles along US 190. The wooden crossarms were snapped off. Also, power lines were blown down. The estimated wind speed was 85 to 100 mph. The time of damage is based on radar.

Delayed report: The NWS conducted a storm survey. There were many windows broken from the large hail at a house and a few outbuildings. Also, lots of golf ball size hail and the hail lasted 20 to 30 minutes.

Delayed Report: The NWS conducted a storm survey. There was major damage to an outbuilding. the roof was blown off an thrown about 100 feet. Also, many tree branches were broken. The time is based on radar.
